characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: Adult male narrator; intelligent, restrained, dry, observant. Cinematic without sounding theatrical. He lets the unease come from the prose rather than announcing it.
characters.performance: Measured at the excavation; gradually cooler and tighter during descent; slower and more spacious inside the tomb; controlled shock after Kurash dies.

characters.name: Zik
characters.description: Experienced, dry, skeptical, technically precise. He notices details other people miss and rarely wastes words. Emotion is present but usually held under control.
characters.performance: Underplay jokes. Technical explanations should sound effortless, not lectured. Tighten noticeably around his father's compass and journal. Final 'that's new' is shock hidden behind dry control.

characters.name: Balag
characters.description: Large, grounded, dry-humored, cautious. Sounds like a man who trusts weight, stone and practical experience more than theories.
characters.performance: Low-key and economical. Humor lands because he does not perform it. His ward/religion exchange carries real unease under the joke. 'Kurash' is a genuine warning, not anger.

characters.name: Enhedu
characters.description: Quick, sharp, observant, amused by the men without becoming flippant. She is alert to material details and danger.
characters.performance: Keep teasing lines understated. As the group descends, humor narrows into focused attention. 'Then they chose the wrong door' should be confident, not cartoonishly fearless.

characters.name: Kurash
characters.description: Young, eager, curious, hungry for a better life, not stupid. He asks too many questions because he wants to learn and wants what the expedition might buy him.
characters.performance: Faster than the others, but natural. Excitement increases around the treasure. His last choices should sound like rationalization and temptation, not villainy.

characters.name: Bel-iddin
characters.role: Zik's father; remembered teacher and journal voice
characters.description: Older, precise, intimate, grave. A teacher who expects Zik to think. His remembered advice is calm certainty; the journal carries more urgency.
characters.performance: Memory lines are dry and instructional. First two journal lines are intimate and grave. The final second-door warning is the same man under strain: urgent, pressed, but still intelligible.

characters.name: Dead King
characters.role: Crowned skeleton in the sealed tomb
characters.description: Ancient, dry, unnervingly calm. This voice is reference-conditioned by Chatterbox Nano from a real gravelly whispered performance rather than manufactured with post-processing noise.
characters.performance: Nearly whispered, brittle and scratchy from the actual reference performance. Threatening because it is quiet and certain. 'Zikir Ashur.' should sound like damaged vocal cords forcing out a name. Leave a long beat after it.
